The *Bākulattheragāthā* (Thag 3.3) is a canonical poem located in the *Theragāthā* of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. It has been translated into multiple modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral]. The work is also referenced in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37, *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*) [SuttaCentral].

In terms of textual parallels and reuse, the text demonstrates extensive structural sharing within the Pali canon. SuttaCentral notes a full parallel with the *Hāritattheragāthā* (Thag 3.15), which DharmaNexus corroborates through a comprehensive passage alignment across segments §0.1–3.5 with 0.97 similarity [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral further records passage-level parallels with the *Ujjhānasaññisutta* (SN 1.35), the *Subhūtattheragāthā* (Thag 5.2), and several Jātaka verses, specifically the *Succajajātaka* (Ja 320), the *Hirijātaka* (Ja 363), and the *Āsaṅkajātaka* (Ja 380), as well as a resembling parallel in the *Varuṇajātaka* (Ja 71) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects recurring textual reuse in the Pali commentarial tradition, matching verses §1.1–3.5 in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and §2.1–2.4 in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language alignments with Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan texts are registered by DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].
